args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED IN ANTICIPATION OF LITIGATION AND NEGOTIATION

MARKUP ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM
CFIUS NATIONAL SECURITY AGREEMENT ("NSA")

To:      Deal Team / Transaction Committee
From:    International Trade & Sanctions Practice Group
Re:      Counterparty Markup Analysis — Risk-Prioritized Memo with Recommendations and Counter-Draft Language
Date:    [Current Date]
Status:  FINAL — reflect the controlling instruction in the current deal correspondence

---------------------------------------------------------------------
I. SCOPE AND DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
---------------------------------------------------------------------
This memorandum analyzes the counterparty's markup of the draft CFIUS National Security Agreement (the "NSA") against the base materials, supporting schedules/exhibits, and controlling deal-team instructions for this international trade sanctions matter. Each materially deviating provision is reconciled against the operative record and is accompanied by a risk priority, a recommendation (accept / concede / reject / counter), and counter-draft language.

Documents reviewed (each read in full):
1. Deal materials / draft NSA — base operative record (Matter File 20);
2. Counterparty markup to the NSA;
3. Schedules and exhibits — disclosure schedules 3.7 and 5.2 and survival matrix Exhibit B;
4. Deal team correspondence — controlling instruction (latest message controls over superseded earlier messages).

The unrelated administrative file misfiled into this matter's folder was identified as a distractor and was not relied on.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF RISK PROFILE
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The counterparty accepted most firm-standard provisions, but the markup introduces four material deviations. Reconciling those deviations against the base materials, the schedules, and the governing deal-team instruction produces the following risk-prioritized treatment:

RISK 1 (CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY): Shortening of the survival period for the core representations. The controlling instruction treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This must be rejected. Exhibit B's survival matrix is contradicted by the markup and must be held at full length for the core reps.

RISK 2 (HIGH): New Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") carve-outs for "regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue." Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these carve-outs directly; the carve-outs would permit the counterparty to walk away precisely when the pending inquiries materialize. Must be rejected or narrowed to exclude the disclosed/pending inquiries.

RISK 3 (HIGH-MEDIUM): Silent reduction of the indemnification cap. Read together with Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities), the reduced cap silently shifts retained-liability risk to the client. Must be countered back to the firm-standard cap (or otherwise expressly reconciled with Schedule 5.2).

RISK 4 (CONCEDE PER CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION): Conversion of the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. The client has instructed that this conversion is conceded. No counter-draft required; confirm in the conformed draft.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
III. MATERIAL CHANGE ANALYSIS AND COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE
---------------------------------------------------------------------

--- RISK 1 — SURVIVAL PERIOD REDUCTION (CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY) ---

DEVIATION. The markup introduces a new/revised limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations, contradicting the survival matrix set out in Exhibit B of the base materials.

RECONCILIATION. Exhibit B establishes the negotiated survival matrix for the indemnification obligations. The markup's shortened limitation period would extinguish indemnification claims for the core reps before the negotiated window closes. This conflicts with the controlling deal-team instruction, which treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue, and supersedes the earlier (opposite) instruction in the thread.

RECOMMENDATION: REJECT — walk-away issue. Hold Exhibit B's survival matrix in full for the core representations. Any concession on survival is outside the client's authorized fallback.

COUNTER-DRAFT:
"Section [X]. Survival. The representations and warranties of the Parties set forth in Section [3] (representations of [SELLER]) and Section [4] (representations of [BUYER]) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B (the "Survival Matrix"), and no provision of this Agreement, including any general survival or limitation period contained in Section [11] (indemnification), shall operate to shorten, waive, or otherwise reduce those survival periods. The Parties acknowledge that the Survival Matrix controls over any conflicting general limitation or survival language in this Agreement."

Also conform Exhibit B: "Exhibit B — Survival Matrix — is hereby retained in the form attached to the base draft and is not amended by the counterparty markup."

--- RISK 2 — MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR PENDING REGULATORY ACTION (HIGH) ---

DEVIATION. The markup amends the definition of Material Adverse Effect to add carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

RECONCILIATION. Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that fall squarely within the described carve-out. If adopted, the carve-out would treat the materialization of those pending inquiries as a non-MAE, permitting the counterparty to proceed (or contend there was no MAE) notwithstanding a material adverse regulatory development—precisely the scenario most likely to arise. This converts a negotiated MAE standard into a walk-away/substantive-escape valve adverse to the client.

RECOMMENDATION: REJECT the regulatory-action carve-out as drafted. Counter with a carve-out that is expressly carved-back for the matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7 and for any pending, threatened, or reasonably foreseeable regulatory action of the same character as the disclosed inquiries.

COUNTER-DRAFT:
"Section [X]. Definition — Material Adverse Effect. The definition of 'Material Adverse Effect' shall not include, and shall be deemed not to have occurred as a result of, any effect arising from or attributable to any action, inquiry, investigation, or proceeding taken or commenced by any Governmental Authority, in each case to the extent such effect (a) was disclosed on Schedule 3.7, (b) arises out of any pending, threatened, or reasonably foreseeable Governmental Authority action, inquiry, investigation, or proceeding of the same character as, or relating to, any matter disclosed on Schedule 3.7, or (c) results from a change in applicable law or regulation that is generally applicable to the industry; provided, however, that this carve-out shall not apply to the extent such effect has resulted in, or could reasonably be expected to result in, a material adverse change in the business, assets, liabilities, condition, or results of operations of the [target] that is disproportionate to the effect on similarly situated industry participants (the 'Disproportionality Exception')."

--- RISK 3 — SILENT INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION (HIGH-MEDIUM) ---

DEVIATION. The markup silently reduces the indemnification cap relative to the firm-standard/base cap.

RECONCILIATION. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift to the client. Reducing the cap without adjusting Schedule 5.2, and without express acknowledgment, transfers risk to the client that was not negotiated. Because the base materials (and the schedules) make the scheduled exceptions controlling, the reduced cap must be reconciled against Schedule 5.2 before it can be accepted.

RECOMMENDATION: COUNTER back to the base/firm-standard indemnification cap, and expressly tie the cap to Schedule 5.2. Alternatively, if the client is willing to consider a reduced cap, require a corresponding conforming revision to Schedule 5.2 and express acknowledgment, and accept only in writing by the transaction committee.

COUNTER-DRAFT:
"Section [X]. Indemnification — Cap. The aggregate liability of [INDEMNITOR] for all indemnification obligations under this Article [X] shall not exceed [● (insert base/firm-standard cap)] (the 'Cap'), provided that the Cap shall not apply to (a) fraud or intentional misrepresentation, (b) breach of the fundamental representations set forth in Section [3] and Section [4], or (c) the retained liabilities described on Schedule 5.2. The Cap is set with reference to, and does not reduce the scope of, the retained liabilities disclosed on Schedule 5.2, which shall continue to be borne by [INDEMNITOR] as set forth therein. For the avoidance of doubt, the indemnification cap set forth in the base draft NSA is retained and not reduced."

--- RISK 4 — BASKET CONVERSION (CONCEDE) ---

DEVIATION. The markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

RECONCILIATION. The controlling deal-team instruction concedes the basket conversion. This is consistent with the client's direction and does not require counter-drafting. The conformed draft should reflect the tipping-basket mechanics.

RECOMMENDATION: ACCEPT (concede), per the controlling instruction.

CONFIRMED LANGUAGE (for the conformed draft):
"Section [X]. Indemnification — Basket. [INDEMNITOR] shall not be required to make payment in respect of any indemnification obligations under this Article [X] (other than in respect of fraud, intentional misrepresentation, and fundamental representations) until the aggregate amount of all Losses for which [INDEMNITOR] would otherwise be liable exceeds [●] (the 'Basket'), and thereafter [INDEMNITOR] shall be liable for all such Losses from the first dollar (a tipping basket)."

---------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. SUPPORTING MATERIALS RECONCILIATION
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The disclosure schedules and exhibits qualify the base materials and control over general statements. The following reconciliations are required:

• Schedule 3.7 (Pending Regulatory Inquiries): Two pending regulatory inquiries intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. The MAE carve-out must be narrowed (RISK 2) so that the disclosed and like-kind inquiries are expressly carved back and subject to the Disproportionality Exception.

• Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities): The retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 are directly implicated by the markup's indemnification changes. Any indemnification-cap reduction must be reconciled against Schedule 5.2 (RISK 3); the retained-liability scope must be unchanged by the cap revision.

• Exhibit B (Survival Matrix): The survival matrix in Exhibit B controls over the general limitation/survival language. The markup's shortened limitation period contradicts Exhibit B and must be rejected (RISK 1); Exhibit B is to be retained unchanged.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
V. CLOSING RECOMMENDATION
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Subject to final capital/structural markups, we recommend the following posture for the next round of negotiations:
1. REJECT the survival-period reduction (walk-away); hold Exhibit B in full.
2. REJECT the MAE regulatory carve-out as drafted; counter with carve-back language tied to Schedule 3.7 plus the Disproportionality Exception.
3. COUNTER the indemnification cap back to the base level and preserve Schedule 5.2's retained-liability scope.
4. CONCEDE the basket conversion (deductible → tipping), per client instruction.

The conformed counter-draft language above should be inserted at the corresponding sections and tied to the schedules/exhibits to preserve the negotiated risk allocation.

Please advise if the firm-standard cap figure and Exhibit B survival durations are confirmed for insertion as the bracketed terms.

[Associate], International Trade & Sanctions Practice Group
